Verdict: ACCEPTThe argument proves the stated all-size graph theorem under the actual hypotheses. I find no failing mathematical step in the all-subsets rank inequality, the two removed component types, the simultaneous exchange choices, or the rounding.The decisive point is that the two potentially deficient quotient components saturate their supporting squares. That forces them to be closed components of  $A\cup B$ , even when they arise from an arbitrary proper subset of exceptional-cycle labels. The removals therefore justify the full family of rank inequalities needed for a single rainbow forest.Here is the detailed audit.1. The all-subsets rank inequality is validLet  $Q_1,\ldots,Q_s$  denote the  $A$ -squares, and work after the stated removals.Every residual  $E_i$  is nonempty and connected on its supportThe sequence of squares visited by an owner cycle gives a connected projected walk. Discarding loop edges preserves connectivity between distinct supporting squares.If an owner cycle occupies only one square, it has at most four vertices. Since  $B$  is simple and its cycles are even, that cycle must be a  $C_4$  occupying all four vertices of the square. Its vertices have no  $B$ -edges leaving the cycle, and the square has no  $A$ -edges leaving it. Thus it is a closed four-vertex component of  $A\cup B$ , already removed.Consequently every residual exceptional cycle has a nonempty  $E_i$ , connected on its entire square support. For every label subset  $J$ , each label in  $J$  therefore belongs wholly to one connected component of
$$E_J=\bigcup_{i\in J}E_i.$$
This observation makes the componentwise counting legitimate. Ambient isolated quotient vertices carrying no label contribute zero rank and require no estimate.The capacity estimate uses the actual hypotheses correctlyConsider a connected component of  $E_J$ , containing  $x$  cycles of order  $4\bmod 6$ ,  $y$  cycles of order  $2\bmod 6$ , and  $v$  supporting squares.The corresponding owner cycles are distinct components of  $B$ , so their vertex sets are disjoint. They use at least
$$4x+8y$$
vertices, all lying in these  $v$  squares. Hence
$$4v\ge 4x+8y,\qquad v\ge x+2y.$$
The lower bound of eight for a  $2\bmod 6$  cycle is justified: simplicity excludes a two-vertex cycle.Since the projected component is connected, its graphic rank is  $v-1$ , including when it has parallel edges. The proposed comparison is
$$x+2y-1-\frac{2x+y}{3}
=\frac{x+5y-3}{3}.$$
Thus it holds whenever  $x+5y\ge3$ . For a component carrying at least one label, the only remaining possibilities are
$$(x,y)=(1,0),\qquad (x,y)=(2,0).$$
The two exceptions are closed even for arbitrary  $J$ For  $(x,y)=(1,0)$ , the only troublesome value is  $v=1$ . The preceding argument shows that this is precisely a removed four-vertex component. Thus a residual component of this type has
$$v\ge2,\qquad v-1\ge1\ge\frac23.$$
For  $(x,y)=(2,0)$ , the only troublesome value is  $v=2$ . In that case the two owner cycles have at least eight vertices, while the two squares have exactly eight available vertices. Equality is forced throughout:Both owner cycles are  $C_4$ 's.Together they occupy every vertex of the two squares.No other owner component has a vertex in either square.No  $B$ -edge leaves these vertices, because the two cycles are components of  $B$ .No  $A$ -edge leaves them, because they are the union of two complete  $A$ -squares.Moreover, connectivity of the projected component implies connectivity of the union of these two squares and their owner edges. They therefore constitute exactly a closed eight-vertex connected component of the removed type.This is the crucial all-subsets check. Labels omitted from  $J$  cannot create an external connection in this exceptional case, because the selected cycles already occupy every vertex of the supporting squares.Thus, in the residual, a component with  $(x,y)=(2,0)$  has
$$v\ge3,\qquad v-1\ge2\ge\frac43.$$
Adding these valid estimates over all components of  $E_J$  gives
$$\operatorname{rank}(E_J)
\ge \sum_{i\in J}d_i$$
for every  $J$ , including  $J=\varnothing$ .There is no unsupported passage from a full-label estimate to an all-subsets estimate.2. The rainbow-rank formula and its use are soundThe self-contained proof of the independent-representative criterion has the needed contraction properties.Tight-subset branchSuppose a nonempty proper label subset  $J$  is tight, and let  $I$  be its independent representatives. Then
$$|I|=|J|=\operatorname{rank}(E_J),$$
so  $I$  spans  $E_J$ .For a subset  $K$  of the remaining labels, the rank in the contracted matroid is
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{rank}_{M/I}(E_K\setminus I)
&=\operatorname{rank}_M(E_K\cup I)-|I|\\
&=\operatorname{rank}_M(E_K\cup E_J)-|J|\\
&\ge |K|.
\end{aligned}$$
The middle equality follows precisely because  $I$  spans  $E_J$ . This supplies the induction hypothesis for all remaining label subsets.No-tight-subset branchIf no nonempty proper subset is tight, every such subset has integer rank at least its cardinality plus one. Choose a nonloop representative for the last label and contract it. Each relevant rank decreases by at most one, leaving all required inequalities intact. The one-label case is immediate.Thus the full-representative criterion is proved.Dummy elementsFor complete precision, the dummy construction can be written as follows: take the direct sum of the original matroid with a free matroid on a new  $k$ -element set  $Z$ , and replace each  $E_i$  by  $E_i\cup Z$ .Then, for nonempty  $J$ ,
$$\operatorname{rank}(E_J\cup Z)
=\operatorname{rank}(E_J)+k
\ge |J|.$$
A full independent representative family uses at most  $k$  dummy elements, so it supplies at least  $c-k$  original representatives. Combined with the immediate upper bounds, this proves
$$r=\min_{J\subseteq[c]}
\left(c-|J|+\operatorname{rank}(E_J)\right).$$
Finally, writing  $d=\sum_i d_i$ , every expression in this minimum satisfies
$$\begin{aligned}
c-|J|+\operatorname{rank}(E_J)
&\ge c-|J|+\sum_{i\in J}d_i\\
&=d+\sum_{i\notin J}(1-d_i)\\
&\ge d.
\end{aligned}$$
Therefore
$$r\ge\lceil d\rceil.$$
This yields one simultaneously realizable rainbow forest of the required size.3. The exchanges can be constructed, and their choices are independentThe prescribed-edge exchange can also be checked directly, so the graph theorem need not depend on an unstated construction.Number a cycle’s vertices  $0,\ldots,n-1$ , taking the prescribed edge to be  $01$ . A binary word records the selected vertices.For  $n=3m+1$ , use
$$10(101)^{m-1}10,
\qquad
01(101)^{m-1}10.$$
Both words have length  $n$ , weight  $2m$ , and no cyclic occurrence of  $111$ . They differ exactly at positions  $0,1$ .For  $n=3m+2$ , use
$$10(101)^m,
\qquad
01(101)^m.$$
These have length  $n$ , weight  $2m+1$ , and the same two properties.On a cycle of length at least four, a selected set is dissociated exactly when no three cyclically consecutive vertices are all selected. Summing that constraint over all cyclic triples gives
$$3|D|\le2n.$$
The displayed words attain  $\lfloor2n/3\rfloor$ , so they are maximum dissociation sets. They cover both exceptional residue classes, including the  $C_4$  case.Now take a rainbow forest. Its selected edges have distinct owner-cycle labels, hence lie in distinct components of  $B$ . Choosing either maximum set in each selected cycle preserves the total maximum owner size.A selected cycle may touch squares beyond the two endpoint squares of its chosen edge. That causes no coupling: its two maximum sets agree at every vertex except those endpoints. Each switch therefore toggles exactly the two endpoint-square parities.The choices are genuinely independent because they act on disjoint owner components. Several switches may affect one square, but their parity changes simply add modulo two.4. The forest parity argument and square rounding are correctFix initial choices of maximum owner sets. On a tree  $T$  of the chosen forest, the available parity changes are the image of its incidence matrix over  $\mathbb F_2$ .For a tree, this image consists exactly of the vectors with even coordinate sum. Equivalently, the reachable square-parity vectors are precisely those with the same total parity as the initial vector. The claimed leaf-to-root procedure realizes any such target.For a tree on  $v$  squares:If the all-one vector has the required parity, all  $v$  intersections can be made odd.Otherwise, a vector with exactly one zero has the required parity, giving  $v-1$  odd intersections.Summing over tree components gives at least
$$\sum_T(|V(T)|-1)=r$$
odd square intersections.For the resulting maximum owner set  $D$ , let
$$k_Q=|D\cap Q|,
\qquad
o=\#\{Q:k_Q\text{ is odd}\}.$$
Each  $A$ -square has two independent opposite-vertex classes. Taking the larger class within  $D\cap Q$  gives at least  $\lceil k_Q/2\rceil$  vertices. These choices combine across the disjoint squares, and the resulting set remains  $B$ -dissociated because it is a subset of  $D$ .Consequently
$$\begin{aligned}
|S|
&\ge \sum_Q\left\lceil\frac{k_Q}{2}\right\rceil\\
&=\frac{\beta_2(B)+o}{2}\\
&\ge \left\lceil\frac{\beta_2(B)+r}{2}\right\rceil.
\end{aligned}$$
The last step is valid even when  $\beta_2(B)+r$  is odd. The middle expression is an integer, since
$$o\equiv \sum_Q k_Q=\beta_2(B)\pmod2,$$
and  $o\ge r$ .Thus there is no duplicated square gain, parity inconsistency, or unsupported rounding step.5. Both removed component types have the claimed selectionsFour verticesThe owner  $C_4$  and the  $A$ -square need only have the same four-vertex support; their edge sets may differ.Any  $A$ -opposite pair is  $A$ -independent. Every two-vertex set induces a simple graph of maximum degree at most one, so the pair is also  $B$ -dissociated. The claimed selection of size two is valid.Eight verticesConsider a connected component comprising two  $A$ -squares and two owner  $C_4$ 's.If either owner cycle were contained in one square, it would occupy all four vertices of that square and make the square a separate closed component. This contradicts connectivity of the eight-vertex component. Hence both owner cycles cross the two squares, and a crossing owner edge exists.There is also a direct check of the claimed size-three construction. A maximum owner set has total size four. Therefore its two square-intersection parities agree: they are either both even or both odd. Switching across the chosen crossing edge toggles both parities, so one exchange choice makes both odd.The intersection sizes must then be  $1$  and  $3$ . They supply independent subsets of sizes  $1$  and  $2$ , respectively, producing three compatible vertices.Because the removed pieces are whole components of  $A\cup B$ , their selections can be united with each other and with the residual selection.6. The deficit count and final ceilings are validFor a path on  $n$  vertices,
$$\beta_2(P_n)=\left\lceil\frac{2n}{3}\right\rceil.$$
One obtains the upper bound by partitioning into consecutive triples, with a possible final block of one or two vertices; the repeating pattern  $110$ , followed by the appropriate prefix, attains it.For a cycle,
$$\beta_2(C_n)=\left\lfloor\frac{2n}{3}\right\rfloor,$$
as checked above for the exceptional cases, with repeating  $110$  attaining the bound when  $3\mid n$ .Thus the relevant contributions are:Owner componentContribution relative to  $2n/3$ PathNonnegative surplusCycle of order  $0\bmod6$  $0$ Cycle of order  $4\bmod6$ Deficit  $2/3$ Cycle of order  $2\bmod6$ Deficit  $1/3$ Let  $N_0$  be the residual vertex count. Then
$$\beta_2(B_{\mathrm{res}})\ge\frac{2N_0}{3}-d,
\qquad
r\ge\lceil d\rceil\ge d.$$
Hence
$$\beta_2(B_{\mathrm{res}})+r\ge\frac{2N_0}{3},$$
and the forest lemma gives
$$|S_{\mathrm{res}}|
\ge
\left\lceil\frac{\beta_2(B_{\mathrm{res}})+r}{2}\right\rceil
\ge
\left\lceil\frac{N_0}{3}\right\rceil.$$
Suppose  $a$  four-vertex components and  $h$  eight-vertex components were removed. The total selection has size at least
$$\left\lceil\frac{N_0}{3}\right\rceil+2a+3h.$$
This integer is at least
$$\frac{N_0}{3}+\frac{4a}{3}+\frac{8h}{3}
=\frac{N}{3},$$
so it is at least  $\lceil N/3\rceil$ .The empty-label, empty-residual, and empty-graph cases are consistent with these bounds.Publication clarifications and scopeI would make three conventions explicit in the written proof:“Coincident  $C_4$ ” means the same four-vertex support; identical  $A$ - and  $B$ -edge sets are unnecessary.Every residual exceptional  $E_i$  is nonempty, so each label lies wholly in one component of  $E_J$ .The dummy extension is the direct sum with a free matroid on the  $k$  new dummy elements.These clarifications do not change the argument.The proof also supplies an actual construction: the representative induction supplies the rainbow forest, the displayed binary words supply the exchange pairs, leaf-to-root toggles realize the target parities, and choosing the larger opposite class in each square supplies  $S$ .Accordingly, the abstract theorem removes the owner-size hypothesis for auxiliary graphs that are disjoint unions of squares. With the stipulated exact square normalization identifying  $N=8b$ , its physical consequence is
$$\boxed{\beta_I\ge\left\lceil\frac{8b}{3}\right\rceil.}$$
The earlier sharp-template assertion is separate from, and unused in, this proof.
